MetricExtractor.description: Identifies which metric to extract from CompanyMetrics.

oneOf.description: A custom metric key from the `custom` map.

Multiple.description:
Valuation multiple.

Enterprise value multiples use EV as the numerator. Equity multiples
use market capitalization or share price. Credit multiples use spread
or yield as the numerator and a fundamental metric as denominator.

oneOf.description: Dividend Yield (dividend / price, expressed as a ratio)
Spread per turn of leverage (OAS / (Debt / EBITDA))

PeerFilter.description:
Criteria for filtering companies into a peer set.

All criteria are AND-ed: a company must satisfy every non-empty
constraint to be included. For OR semantics across sectors or
ratings, supply multiple values in the respective `Vec`.

Every field may be omitted from the serde document: an omitted list or
bound is no constraint, so `{}` (the [`Default`]) accepts every company.
Unknown keys are rejected, so a misspelt criterion is an error rather than
a silently dropped screen.

countries.description: ISO country codes to include (meta key: "country").

excluded_tags.description: Excluded attribute tags (none may be present).

gics_industries.description: GICS industry codes to include (meta key: "gics_industry").

gics_sectors.description: GICS sector codes to include (meta key: "gics_sector").

ratings.description: Credit rating bands to include (meta key: "rating").

required_tags.description: Required attribute tags (all must be present).

PeriodBasis.description: Time basis for computing a valuation multiple.

oneOf.description: Next twelve months (forward consensus or forecast).
Custom period identified by a label (e.g., "FY2025E").

ScoreDirection.description:
Rich/cheap sign convention for a scoring dimension's Y metric.

Determines how a higher-than-peers Y value maps onto the composite
score (positive = cheap). Spread- and yield-like metrics are cheap
when high ([`HigherIsCheap`](Self::HigherIsCheap)); valuation
multiples (P/E, EV/EBITDA) are rich when high
([`HigherIsRich`](Self::HigherIsRich)).

The direction is applied consistently to both the regression-residual
path and the univariate z-score path. The default,
`HigherIsCheap`, matches the historical regression-path convention
(positive residual = actual spread above fitted fair spread = cheap).

oneOf.description: Higher Y than peers means the subject is cheap (spread-like metrics).
Higher Y than peers means the subject is rich (multiple-like metrics).

ScoringDimension.description: Configuration for a single rich/cheap scoring dimension.

direction.description:
Rich/cheap sign convention for the Y metric (default:
[`ScoreDirection::HigherIsCheap`], i.e. spread-like).

weight.description: Finite, non-negative relative weight in the composite score; zero disables it.

x_extractor.description:
Optional explanatory metric for single-factor regression.
Omit it to score the dependent metric against its peer distribution.

y_extractor.description: How to extract the Y variable (dependent) from CompanyMetrics.

description: Peer filter, period basis, scoring dimensions and multiple columns for a relative value report.

dimensions.description:
Scoring dimensions, in the order the report returns them. May be empty
when `multiples` is not.

filter.description:
Screen applied to the universe. Omitted, every other company is a peer.
Any [`PeerFilter`] field may be omitted, meaning no constraint on it; an
unknown field is rejected.

multiples.description:
Columns of the comps table, in the order the report returns them. May be
empty when `dimensions` is not.

period_basis.description:
Period basis the supplied metrics are stated on. It labels the report;
the metrics are used as given.
